claims.text: LayoutBuilder calls its builder with the BoxConstraints its parent gives it during layout, so the returned subtree can depend on the available size.
ProductCatalog@stage-1: below maxWidth 600 it returns ListView.builder of ProductTile; otherwise GridView.builder with crossAxisCount = floor(maxWidth / 300) and mainAxisExtent 72, same ProductTile.
At stage-1 no screen uses ProductCatalog; ProductListScreen still builds its own ListView.
product_catalog_test.dart places ProductCatalog in a SizedBox of width 360 or 900; at 360 it finds a ListView and no GridView, at 900 a GridView with two ProductTiles; the tests pass.
Column counts from the code: 600 -> 2, 900 -> 3, 1250 -> 4; 599 and 360 -> ListView.
Deciding a layout from the whole screen size breaks when a widget gets a different amount of room (narrow window, side panel, rotated tablet); deciding from its constraints keeps working.

self_check.notes: Code added to the example repo by owner decision (DECISIONS.md §3, 2026-09-28); ProductCatalog is not yet used by a screen, said openly. No device breakpoints or orientation handling (depth_notes).
